en: Dhammasaṅgaṇī 2:
Exposition 2.1 Section on the Arising of Consciousness (Cittuppādakaṇḍa)
2.1.6. Twelve Unwholesome States Which states are unwholesome?
At whatever time an unwholesome consciousness has arisen that is accompanied by joy and associated with wrong view...
Whether it be a visible-form object, a sound object, a smell object, a taste object, a tangible-object, or a mental-object,
or whatever else [is taken as] the basis— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is rapture, and there is pleasure.
There is [the faculty of] faith, there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of energy, there is the faculty of concentration, there is the faculty of mind,
there is the faculty of mental pleasure, there is the life-faculty, there is wrong view, there is wrong intention,
there is wrong effort, there is wrong concentration, there is the power of energy, there is the power of concentration.
There is the power of moral shamelessness, there is the power of moral fearlessness, there is greed, there is delusion, there is covetousness, there is wrong view,
there is moral shamelessness, there is moral fearlessness, there is serenity, there is exertion, there is non-distraction;
or whatever other dependent-arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time.
These states are unwholesome.
What on that occasion is contact?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted, the state of being contacted.
This, at that time, is contact.
What, at that time, is feeling?

That which, at that time, is born of the contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element; the mental gratification, the mental pleasure, the pleasant and happy experience born of mental contact—that is, the pleasant and happy feeling born of mental contact. This, at that time, is feeling.
This, at that time, is feeling.
What, at that time, is perception?
That which, at that time, is perception born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element—the perceiving, the state of having perceived.
This, at that time, is perception.
What, at that time, is volition?
That which, at that time, is volition born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element, the state of intending, the state of having intended—this, at that time, is volition.
At that time, this is volition.
What is the mind at that time?

That which at that time is the mind, the intellect, the mental faculty, the heart, the clarity, the mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding element of mind-consciousness.
This is the state of mind at that time.
What is the applied thought (vitakka) at that time?
It is whatever at that time is reasoning, applied thought, intention, absorption, focused application, the directing of the mind, and wrong intention.
At that time, this is what constitutes applied thought (*vitakka*).
What at that time is sustained thought (*vicāra*)?
That which at that time is moving about, sustained movement, following through, close investigation, the continuous threading of the mind, and the constant scrutiny—that is sustained thought.
At that time, this is what constitutes sustained thought (vicāra).
What at that time is rapture (pīti)?
It is that which at that time is rapture, gladness, rejoicing, exultation, laughter, mirth, elation, buoyancy, and mental satisfaction.
This, at that time, is rapture (pīti).
What, at that time, is pleasure (sukha)?

That which at that time is mental well-being, mental pleasure, a pleasant and pleasurable feeling born of mind-contact, a pleasant and pleasurable sensation born of mind-contact—this, at that time, is pleasure.
This, at that time, is happiness.
What, at that time, is one-pointedness of mind?

It is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-wavering, non-distraction, unperturbed state of mind, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration at that time.
At that time, this is one-pointedness of mind.
What, at that time, is the faculty of energy?
It is that which, at that time, is the arousal of mental energy, exertion, striving, endeavor, effort, perseverance, and fortitude.
Stamina, fortitude, unrelaxed persistence, non-abandonment of zeal, non-abandonment of the burden, the exertion of the burden,
energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy,
and right effort— this, at that time, is the faculty of energy.
What on that occasion is the faculty of concentration?

That which on that occasion is stability of mind, steadfastness, firmness, imperturbability, non-distraction, mental composure, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration—
this on that occasion is the faculty of concentration.
What on that occasion is the faculty of mind (manindriya)?

That which on that occasion is consciousness, mind, mentation, heart, lucidity, mind, the mind-base, the faculty of mind, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the element of mind-consciousness born thereof—
this on that occasion is the faculty of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of mental joy (*somanassindriya*)?
That which on that occasion is mental well-being, mental pleasure, a pleasant and happy feeling born of mental contact, a pleasant and happy sensation born of mental contact—
this on that occasion is the faculty of mental joy.
What on that occasion is the life-faculty?
That which, for those immaterial states, is the life-span, the persistence, the subsistence, the maintenance, the going-on, the occurrence,
the upkeep, the vitality, the life-faculty— this on that occasion is the life-faculty.
What at that time is wrong view? Whatever at that time is a view,
a resort to views, a thicket of views, a wilderness of views, a distortion of views, a vacillation of views,
a fetter of views, a seizing, a fixation, an adherence, a misapprehension, a wrong path.
The wrong path, wrongness, a sectarian standpoint, and a perverted grasp—
at that time, this is what constitutes wrong view.
What at that time is wrong intention?
Whatever at that time is reasoning, thought, intention, absorption, sustained application, the directing of the mind, and wrong intention—
this, at that time, is wrong intention.
What, at that time, is wrong effort?
Whatever at that time is the arousal of mental energy, exertion, striving, endeavor, effort, enthusiasm,
perseverance, fortitude, steadfastness, unfaltering exertion, non-abandonment of desire, non-abandonment of the burden,
the grasping of the burden, energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, and right effort— this is [the factor of enlightenment].
At that time, this is wrong effort.
What at that time is wrong concentration?

That which at that time is the steadiness, stability, steadfastness, non-wavering, non-distraction, state of mental composure, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and wrong concentration—this is wrong concentration at that time.
At that time, this is wrong concentration (*micchā-samādhi*).
What, at that time, is the power of energy (*vīriya-bala*)?
It is that which, at that time, is the arousal of mental energy, the exertion, the striving, the endeavor, the effort, the perseverance, the fortitude.
Stamina, fortitude, unrelaxed perseverance, non-abandonment of desire, non-abandonment of the burden, the exertion of the burden,
energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, and right effort—
this at that time is the power of energy.
What on that occasion is the power of concentration?

That which on that occasion is stability of mind, steadfastness, firmness, non-wavering, non-distraction, mental composure, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration—
this on that occasion is the power of concentration.
What on that occasion is the power of moral shamelessness (ahirikabala)?
That which on that occasion is not ashamed of being ashamed of what should be a cause for shame, and is not ashamed of the attainment of evil, unwholesome states—
this on that occasion is the power of moral shamelessness.
What on that occasion is the power of non-shame (anottappa-bala)?
That which on that occasion is not ashamed where one ought to be ashamed; that which is not ashamed of the attainment of evil, unwholesome states—this on that occasion is the power of non-shame.
What at that time is greed? Whatever at that time is greed,
the state of being greedy, greediness, lust, the state of being lustful, covetousness, greed, the root of unwholesomeness—
this at that time is greed.
What on that occasion is delusion?
That which on that occasion is ignorance, lack of vision, lack of clear comprehension, lack of awakening, lack of full enlightenment,
lack of penetration, lack of fathoming, lack of scrutiny, lack of reflection, lack of direct realization, dullness, and stupidity.
Childishness, lack of clear comprehension, delusion, bewilderment, confusion, ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the underlying tendency to ignorance,
the obsession of ignorance, the snare of ignorance, and delusion as an unwholesome root—
this, at that time, is what constitutes delusion.
What on that occasion is covetousness? Whatever on that occasion is greed,
being greedy, state of being greedy, lust, being lustful, state of being lustful, covetousness, greed, the unwholesome root—
this on that occasion is covetousness.
What at that time is wrong view? Whatever at that time is a view,
a resort to views, a thicket of views, a wilderness of views, a distortion of views, a vacillation of views,
a fetter of views, a seizing, a fixation, an adherence, a misapprehension, a wrong path.
The wrong path, wrongness, a sectarian refuge, and a perverted grasp—
this, at that time, is wrong view.
What, at that time, is moral shamelessness?
That which at that time does not feel shame where there should be shame, and does not feel shame regarding the undertaking of evil, unwholesome states— this, at that time,
is called *ahirika* (shamelessness).
What, at that time, is *anottappa* (fearlessness of wrongdoing)?
That which at that time does not feel shame where one ought to feel shame regarding the undertaking of evil, unwholesome states—
this, at that time, is called lack of moral dread (*anottappa*).
What, at that time, is serenity (*samatha*)?
Whatever at that time is the steadiness, stability, steadfastness, non-wavering, non-distraction, state of non-disturbed mind, serenity, the faculty of concentration,
the power of concentration, and right concentration—
this, at that time, is serenity. What, at that time, is exertion?
Whatever at that time is the arousal of mental energy, the exertion, the striving, the endeavor, the effort,
the perseverance, the fortitude, the steadfastness, the unfaltering persistence, the non-abandonment of zeal, the non-laying down of the burden,
the grasping of the burden, energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, and right effort— this is [the factor of enlightenment].
This, at that time, is exertion.
What, at that time, is non-distraction?

That which at that time is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-wavering, non-distraction, and state of mental non-wavering of the mind; serenity; the faculty of concentration; the power of concentration; and right concentration.
At that time, this is non-distraction;
or whatever other conditionally arisen immaterial phenomena there may be at that time—
these phenomena are unwholesome.
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements,
three nutriments, five faculties, a five-factored jhāna, a four-factored path,
four powers, two roots, one contact …pe… and one mental-object base (dhammāyatana).
there is one element of phenomena (dhammadhātu);
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—these phenomena are unwholesome ... pe ... .
What at that time is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?

Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of energy, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of life, wrong view, wrong intention, wrong effort, wrong concentration, the power of energy, the power of concentration, the power of moral shamelessness... [and so forth].
The power of non-fear-of-blame, greed, delusion, covetousness, wrong view, shamelessness, and non-fear-of-blame; serenity, exertion, and non-distraction;

or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of consciousness—this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations …pe….
These states are unwholesome.
Which states are unwholesome?
At whatever time an unwholesome consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with wrong view, with volitional effort, having visible form as its object … [and so on] … pe … [as before].
Whether it be with mental phenomena as the object or whatever else one has taken as the basis, at that time there is contact … pe … there is non-distraction … pe … these states are unwholesome.
Which states are unwholesome?
At whatever time an unwholesome state of consciousness has arisen that is accompanied by joy,
dissociated from views, and has as its object a visible form, a sound, a smell, a taste, a tangible object, or a mental phenomenon—
or whatever [object] it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, and so forth.
There is perception; there is volition; there is consciousness; there is applied thought; there is sustained thought; there is rapture; there is pleasure;
there is one-pointedness of mind; there is the faculty of energy; there is the faculty of concentration; there is the faculty of mind;
there is the faculty of mental joy; there is the life-faculty; there is wrong intention; there is wrong effort.
There is wrong concentration; there is the power of energy, the power of concentration, the power of moral shamelessness, and the power of moral fearlessness;
there is greed, delusion, covetousness, moral shamelessness, and moral fearlessness;
there is serenity, exertion, and non-distraction.
Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are unwholesome...
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments; there are five faculties; there is five-factored jhāna; there is the three-factored path;
there are four powers; there are two roots; there is one contact … [and so on] … there is one base of mental phenomena;
there is one element of mental phenomena.
Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial states exist at that time—these states are unwholesome. ...
What, at that time, is the aggregate of formations?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, rapture, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of energy, the faculty of concentration, the life-faculty,
wrong intention, wrong effort, wrong concentration, the power of energy, the power of concentration, the power of shamelessness,
the power of fearlessness of wrongdoing, greed, delusion, covetousness, shamelessness, fearlessness of wrongdoing, serenity, exertion, and non-distraction.

Or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness—this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (*saṅkhārakkhandha*). ...
These phenomena are unwholesome.
Which states are unwholesome?

At whatever time an unwholesome consciousness has arisen that is accompanied by joy, dissociated from views, and with volitional activity, having visible form as its object … or mental phenomena as its object,
or whatever else it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact … and so on … there is non-distraction … and so on.
These states are unwholesome.
Which states are unwholesome?
At whatever time an unwholesome consciousness has arisen accompanied by equanimity and associated with wrong view—
Whether it be a visible-form object, a sound object, a smell object, a taste object, a tangible-object, or a mental-object,
or whatever else is taken as the basis— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is equanimity, and one-pointedness of mind.
There is the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of mind, the faculty of equanimity, and the faculty of life;
there is wrong view, wrong intention, wrong effort, and wrong concentration;
there is the power of energy, the power of concentration, the power of shamelessness, and the power of fearlessness of wrongdoing.
There is greed, there is delusion, there is covetousness, there is wrong view, there is moral shamelessness, there is moral recklessness,
there is serenity, there is exertion, there is non-distraction; or whatever other dependent, immaterial states exist at that time.
These states are unwholesome.
What on that occasion is contact?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted, the quality of having contacted.
This, at that time, is contact.
What, at that time, is feeling?

That which, at that time, is born of that same mind-consciousness-element-contact, a mental state that is neither pleasant nor unpleasant, a feeling born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant—this is the feeling born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant.
At that time, this is feeling ... [as before] ... What at that time is equanimity?

That which at that time is mental, neither agreeable nor disagreeable, born of mental contact, an experience of neither-pain-nor-pleasure—that is, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mental contact.
At that time, there is equanimity … [as before] … What, at that time, is the faculty of equanimity?

It is that mental state which, born of mental contact, is neither pleasant nor unpleasant, a feeling of neither-pain-nor-pleasure; it is the feeling of neither-pain-nor-pleasure born of mental contact.
At that time, this is the faculty of equanimity …pe… or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are unwholesome.
At that time, there are four aggregates; there are two bases; there are two elements;
there are three nutriments; there are five faculties; there is a four-factored jhāna; there is a four-factored path;
there are four powers; there are two roots; there is one contact …pe… there is one mental-object base (*dhammāyatana*).
There is one element of phenomena (*dhammadhātu*);
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—these phenomena are unwholesome... [and so on].
What at that time is the aggregate of volitional formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of energy, the faculty of concentration,
the faculty of life, wrong view, wrong intention, wrong effort, wrong concentration, the power of energy, the power of concentration, and the power of moral shamelessness.
The power of non-fear-of-sin, greed, delusion, covetousness, wrong view, shamelessness, and non-fear-of-sin; serenity, exertion, and non-distraction;

or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of consciousness—this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations …pe…
These states are unwholesome.
Which states are unwholesome?

At whatever time an unwholesome consciousness has arisen accompanied by equanimity, associated with wrong view, and prompted, having visible form as its object … [and so on] … these states are unwholesome.
Whether it be with mental objects as its object or whatever else it is directed toward, at that time there is contact … pe … there is non-distraction … pe … these states are unwholesome.
Which states are unwholesome?
At whatever time an unwholesome state of consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from wrong view,
and having as its object a visible form, a sound, a smell, a taste, a tangible object, or a mental phenomenon—
or whatever [object] it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, and so forth.
There is perception, there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is equanimity,
there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of energy, there is the faculty of concentration, there is the faculty of mind,
there is the faculty of equanimity, there is the life-faculty, there is wrong intention, there is wrong effort, there is wrong concentration, and there is the power of energy.

There is energy, there is the power of concentration, there is the power of shamelessness, there is the power of fearlessness of wrongdoing, there is greed, there is delusion, there is covetousness, there is shamelessness,
there is fearlessness of wrongdoing, there is serenity, there is exertion, there is non-distraction; or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time.
These states are unwholesome … [and so on] … At that time there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements,
three nutriments, five faculties, a fourfold jhāna, and a threefold path.
There are four powers, there are two roots, there is one contact …pe… there is one base of mental phenomena,
there is one element of mental phenomena;
or whatever other dependent-originated immaterial phenomena exist at that time.
These states are unwholesome … [as before] … What, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of energy, the faculty of concentration, and the life-faculty.
wrong intention, wrong effort, wrong concentration; the power of energy, the power of concentration, the power of shamelessness, the power of fearlessness of wrongdoing;
greed, delusion, covetousness, shamelessness, fearlessness of wrongdoing; serenity, exertion, and non-distraction;
or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of consciousness.
At that time, this is the aggregate of volitional formations (*saṅkhārakkhandha*) … [as before] … these phenomena are unwholesome.
Which phenomena are unwholesome?
At whatever time an unwholesome state of consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from views, with volitional effort,

having as its object a visible form …pe… a mental phenomenon, or whatever [object] it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact …pe… there is non-distraction …pe… these states are unwholesome.
What states are unwholesome?
At whatever time an unwholesome consciousness has arisen, accompanied by displeasure, associated with aversion,
having as its object a visible form, or a sound, or a smell, or a taste, or a tangible object—
Whether it be a mental object or whatever else he has taken as his basis, at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is suffering, there is one-pointedness of mind, there is the faculty of energy,
there is the faculty of concentration, there is the faculty of mind, and there is the faculty of mental distress.
There is [the faculty of] equanimity, there is the life-faculty, there is wrong intention, there is wrong effort, there is wrong concentration, there is the power of energy,
there is the power of concentration, there is the power of shamelessness, there is the power of fearlessness of wrongdoing,
there is hatred, there is delusion, there is ill will, there is shamelessness, there is fearlessness of wrongdoing, there is serenity, and there is exertion.
There is non-delusion, there is non-distraction;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are unwholesome.
What on that occasion is contact (phassa)?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted,
the state of being contacted— this on that occasion is contact.
What feeling is there at that time?

That which, at that time, is born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element; mental unease, mental pain, an unpleasant and painful experience born of mind-contact—an unpleasant and painful feeling born of mind-contact:
this is the feeling that exists at that time. …pe…
What is suffering at that time?

That which at that time is mental unease, mental suffering, an unpleasant and painful feeling born of mental contact, an unpleasant and painful sensation born of mental contact—this is suffering at that time. …pe…
What on that occasion is the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*)?

That which on that occasion is mental unease, mental suffering, an uneasy and painful feeling born of mental contact, an uneasy and painful sensation born of mental contact—this on that occasion is the faculty of mental grief. …pe…
What at that time is ill-will? That which at that time is ill-will,
being malicious, state of being malicious, malice, being malevolent, state of being malevolent, hostility, opposition, ferocity, abruptness, and mental dissatisfaction—
this at that time is ill-will …pe….
What on that occasion is ill-will (*byāpāda*)?

That which on that occasion is hatred, being hateful, state of being hateful, malevolence, being malevolent, state of being malevolent, hostility, opposition, ferocity, abruptness, and mental dissatisfaction—this on that occasion is ill-will. …pe…
Or whatever other dependent-originated, formless states exist at that time—
these states are unwholesome.
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments, there are five faculties, there is four-factored jhāna, there is a three-factored path,
there are four powers, there are two roots, there is one contact …pe… there is one base of mental phenomena,
there is one element of mental phenomena.
Or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—these phenomena are unwholesome... [etc.
...What, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of energy, the faculty of concentration, the life-faculty,
wrong intention, wrong effort, wrong concentration, the power of energy, the power of concentration, the power of shamelessness,
the power of fearlessness of wrongdoing, hatred, delusion, ill will, shamelessness, fearlessness of wrongdoing, serenity, exertion, and non-distraction.
Or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception,
and excluding the aggregate of consciousness— this, at that time, is the aggregate of mental formations … [as before] … these phenomena are unwholesome.
Which states are unwholesome?

At whatever time an unwholesome consciousness has arisen accompanied by displeasure, associated with aversion, with volitional effort, having visible form as its object … or mental phenomena as its object,
or whatever [object] it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact … and so on … there is non-distraction … and so on.
These phenomena are unwholesome.
Which phenomena are unwholesome?
At whatever time an unwholesome state of consciousness has arisen accompanied by equanimity and associated with doubt—
Whether it be a visible-form object, a sound object, a smell object, a taste object, a tangible-object, or a mental-object,
whatever [object] one has taken up, at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is equanimity, and there is one-pointedness of mind.
There is the faculty of energy, there is the faculty of mind, there is the faculty of equanimity, there is the life-faculty;
there is wrong intention, there is wrong effort, there is the power of energy, there is the power of moral shamelessness, there is the power of moral fearlessness;
there is doubt, there is delusion, there is moral shamelessness, there is moral fearlessness, and there is exertion.
Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are unwholesome.
What, at that time, is contact?
Whatever at that time is contact, the act of contacting, the state of contacting, the state of having contacted—this, at that time, is contact ...
[and so on] ... What, at that time, is one-pointedness of mind?
Whatever at that time is stability of the mind—
this, at that time, is one-pointedness of mind …pe….
What at that time is doubt?
Whatever at that time is doubt, doubting, state of having doubted, perplexity, uncertainty, vacillation,
a forked path, hesitation, holding to various sides, shrinking back, sliding back, lack of penetration, stiffness of mind, mental scarifying—
this at that time is called doubt …pe…
Or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are unwholesome.
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments, four faculties, a fourfold jhāna, a two-factored path,
three powers, one cause, one contact …pe… one base of mental phenomena,
and one element of mental phenomena.
Or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are unwholesome...
[as before] ...What, at that time, is the aggregate of volitional formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of energy, the life-faculty, wrong intention, wrong effort,
the power of energy, the power of shamelessness, the power of fearlessness of wrongdoing, doubt, delusion, shamelessness,

fearlessness of wrongdoing, and exertion; or whatever other dependent, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of consciousness.
At that time, this is the aggregate of volitional formations (*saṅkhārakkhandha*) … [as before] … these phenomena are unwholesome.
Which phenomena are unwholesome?
At whatever time an unwholesome state of consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, associated with restlessness,
having visible form as its object— or whatever else it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception,
there is volition, there is consciousness, there is initial application, there is sustained application, there is equanimity, and there is one-pointedness of mind.
There is the faculty of energy, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of mind, the faculty of equanimity, and the faculty of life;
there is wrong intention, wrong effort, and wrong concentration;
there is the power of energy, the power of concentration, the power of moral shamelessness, and the power of moral fearlessness; there is restlessness and delusion.
There is moral shamelessness, there is moral recklessness, there is serenity, there is exertion, there is non-distraction;
or whatever other dependently arisen immaterial states exist at that time—
these states are unwholesome.
What on that occasion is contact (phassa)?
That which on that occasion is contact, the act of contacting, the state of having contacted,
the state of being touched— this on that occasion is contact …pe….
What on that occasion is restlessness?
That which on that occasion is restlessness of mind, lack of tranquility, mental agitation, and unsteadiness of mind—this on that occasion is restlessness. …pe…
Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are unwholesome.
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments, there are five faculties, there is four-factored jhāna, there is three-factored path,
there are four powers, there is one cause, there is one contact …pe… there is one base of mental phenomena,
there is one element of mental phenomena.
Or whatever other dependent-originated, formless states exist at that time—these states are unwholesome ... [as before] ...
What, at that time, is the aggregate of volitional formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)?
Contact, volition, applied thought, sustained thought, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of energy, the faculty of concentration, the life-faculty,
wrong intention, wrong effort, wrong concentration, the power of energy, the power of concentration, the power of shamelessness, the power of fearlessness of wrongdoing,
restlessness, delusion, shamelessness, fearlessness of wrongdoing, serenity, exertion, and non-distraction.

Or whatever other conditioned, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the feeling aggregate, excluding the perception aggregate, and excluding the consciousness aggregate—this, at that time, is the formations aggregate. ...
These phenomena are unwholesome.
The twelve unwholesome consciousnesses.
